cities.name: Berlin
cities.summary: Germany's capital layers Prussian grandeur, Cold War history and a creative edge across walkable districts, world-class museums and lively neighbourhoods.

clusters.name: Museum Island and Unter den Linden
Brandenburg Gate and Reichstag
attractions: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe

cities.name: Munich
cities.summary: Munich mixes royal architecture, beer-hall tradition and polished museums with easy access to big parks and the Alps.

cities.name: Frankfurt
cities.summary: Frankfurt pairs a striking skyline with restored old-town lanes, excellent museums and one of Germany's best air-rail hubs.

cities.name: Cologne
cities.summary: Cologne is a friendly Rhine city built around its immense Gothic cathedral, museums and an easygoing beer culture.

cities.name: Düsseldorf
cities.summary: Düsseldorf combines smart shopping streets, contemporary architecture and a compact Altstadt right on the Rhine.

cities.name: Hamburg
cities.summary: Hamburg brings together grand merchant architecture, harbor energy, top museums and waterside districts with real character.

cities.name: Stuttgart
cities.summary: Stuttgart is a hill-ringed city of car museums, wine slopes and broad squares backed by strong cultural collections.

cities.name: Dresden
cities.summary: Dresden's rebuilt baroque core, river terraces and major art collections make it one of Germany's most elegant city breaks.

cities.name: Leipzig
cities.summary: Leipzig is a music-rich, fast-changing city known for Bach, grand passages, canals and a lively creative scene.

cities.name: Heidelberg
cities.summary: Heidelberg charms with a romantic riverside setting, Germany's most famous castle ruin and a handsome old university quarter.

cities.name: Nuremberg
cities.summary: Nuremberg blends imperial history, strong museums and one of Europe's best Christmas market traditions inside stout old walls.

clusters.name: WWII and Memory
attractions: Documentation Center Nazi Party Rally Grounds

cities.name: Rothenburg ob der Tauber
cities.summary: Rothenburg is a beautifully preserved medieval town of walls, towers and storybook lanes that feels best after day-trippers leave.

cities.name: Freiburg
cities.summary: Sunny Freiburg offers a lively old town, Black Forest access and a relaxed café culture threaded by little water channels.

cities.name: Hanover
cities.summary: Hanover is an easy city break with formal gardens, lakeside paths and a compact old centre rebuilt around key landmarks.

cities.name: Vienna
cities.summary: Vienna excels at imperial sights, coffeehouse culture, music and museum time, yet still feels graceful and manageable on foot and tram.

cities.name: Salzburg
cities.summary: Salzburg pairs baroque beauty, Mozart heritage and fortress views with easy hill walks and classic café stops.

cities.name: Innsbruck
cities.summary: Innsbruck gives you a Tyrolean old town, mountain panoramas and easy lift access right from a compact urban base.

cities.name: Hallstatt
cities.summary: Hallstatt is a tiny lakeside village with dramatic mountain scenery, photogenic lanes and one of Austria's best-known salt-mine visits.

cities.name: Zell am See
cities.summary: Zell am See combines an attractive lakefront with mountain lifts and easy access to year-round alpine scenery.

cities.name: Kitzbühel
cities.summary: Kitzbühel is a polished Alpine resort famous for ski racing, a handsome centre and easy high-mountain viewpoints.

cities.name: Graz
cities.summary: Graz offers a relaxed historic core, Renaissance courtyards and a stylish modern side around the Mur river.

cities.name: Linz
cities.summary: Linz sits neatly on the Danube and mixes baroque streets with inventive media art and hilltop viewpoints.

cities.name: Wachau Valley
cities.summary: The Wachau is a scenic Danube valley of abbeys, vineyards, river villages and easy wine-focused day trips.

cities.name: Grossglockner
cities.summary: Grossglockner rewards a clear-weather visit with Austria's loftiest mountain scenery, glacier viewpoints and a famed panoramic road.

cities.name: Amsterdam
cities.summary: Amsterdam combines canal views, major museums and lively neighbourhoods with easy cycling and a compact historic core.

cities.name: Rotterdam
cities.summary: Rotterdam stands out for bold postwar architecture, a striking river skyline and one of Europe's biggest ports.

cities.name: The Hague
cities.summary: The Hague offers Dutch political grandeur, excellent art museums and an easy tram hop to the North Sea beach at Scheveningen.

cities.name: Utrecht
cities.summary: Utrecht is an appealing canal city with a towering cathedral precinct, good museums and a less touristy feel than Amsterdam.

cities.name: Delft
cities.summary: Delft is a compact canal town known for Vermeer, blue pottery and one of the Netherlands' prettiest market squares.

cities.name: Haarlem
cities.summary: Haarlem rewards a short stay with fine museums, a graceful market square and quick access to dunes and the coast.

cities.name: Giethoorn
cities.summary: Giethoorn is a quiet canal village best explored by boat, with reed thatch, little bridges and wetland scenery.

cities.name: Eindhoven
cities.summary: Eindhoven is a modern design city where Philips heritage, creative districts and good museums drive the appeal.

cities.name: Maastricht
cities.summary: Maastricht feels distinctly southern, with handsome squares, old churches, caves and a strong food-and-café scene.

cities.name: Zaanse Schans
cities.summary: Zaanse Schans is a photogenic windmill village with classic Dutch craft workshops and quick access from Amsterdam.

cities.name: Vaduz
cities.summary: Vaduz is a tiny capital with museums, vineyard views and a neat main street under the princely castle hill.

cities.name: Schaan
cities.summary: Schaan is Liechtenstein's main town for daily life, good valley views and access to easy mountain paths.

clusters.name: Village Centre and Monastery
attractions: Monastery of the Sisters of the Precious Blood

cities.name: Balzers
cities.summary: Balzers is best known for picture-book Gutenberg Castle and its quiet setting near the Rhine and Swiss border.

cities.name: Triesenberg
cities.summary: Triesenberg brings Walser heritage, broad mountain views and straightforward access up to Liechtenstein's small alpine resort zone.

cities.name: Prague
cities.summary: Prague delivers a dense mix of Gothic, baroque and riverside beauty with major sights packed into an atmospheric historic core.

clusters.name: Old Town and Astronomical Clock
attractions: Church of Our Lady before Týn

cities.name: Český Krumlov
cities.summary: Český Krumlov is a fairytale South Bohemian town with a looping river, a vast castle complex and atmospheric lanes.

cities.name: Karlovy Vary
cities.summary: Karlovy Vary is a handsome spa town of colonnades, hot springs and grand hotels set in wooded western Bohemia.

cities.name: Brno
cities.summary: Brno offers a youthful café scene, strong modernist heritage and an old centre layered with underground sights.

clusters.name: Špilberk and Old Town
attractions: Cathedral of St. Peter and Paul

cities.name: Kutná Hora
cities.summary: Kutná Hora packs striking medieval wealth, a famous bone church and one of Czechia's most rewarding small-town centres.

clusters.name: Sedlec and Bone Church
attractions: Cathedral of the Assumption of Our Lady and Saint John the Baptist

cities.name: Olomouc
cities.summary: Olomouc is a handsome Moravian university city with grand squares, baroque fountains and far fewer tourists than Prague.

cities.name: Pilsen
cities.summary: Pilsen is best known for lager history, but its broad square, cathedral and cellars make it a worthwhile stop.

cities.name: Budapest
cities.summary: Budapest balances grand Danube views, thermal baths, nightlife and layered history across Buda hills and Pest boulevards.

cities.name: Szentendre
cities.summary: Szentendre is a colourful Danube town of baroque lanes, artists' museums and easy day-trip charm from Budapest.

cities.name: Eger
cities.summary: Eger combines a compact baroque centre, a hilltop castle and easy access to cellars pouring Egri Bikavér wines.

cities.name: Debrecen
cities.summary: Debrecen is eastern Hungary's main city, valued for its Calvinist heritage, broad square and green spa park.

cities.name: Pécs
cities.summary: Pécs mixes Roman remains, Ottoman-era landmarks and a sunny southern feel with strong arts spaces.

cities.name: Lake Balaton
cities.summary: Lake Balaton is Central Europe's classic summer lake, mixing beaches, sailing, wine hills and pretty north-shore villages.

cities.name: Hévíz
cities.summary: Hévíz is centred on its famous thermal lake and works well with nearby Keszthely for spa time and palace visits.

cities.name: Warsaw
cities.summary: Warsaw blends reconstructed old-town charm with major museums, broad royal routes and a resilient modern energy.

cities.name: Kraków
cities.summary: Kraków is one of Europe's great short breaks for medieval streets, castle views, Jewish heritage and easy side trips.

cities.name: Wrocław
cities.summary: Wrocław charms with a colourful square, river islands, quirky dwarfs and some of Poland's best family attractions.

clusters.name: Panoramas and Dwarfs
attractions: Panorama of the Battle of Racławice

cities.name: Gdańsk
cities.summary: Gdańsk pairs a richly rebuilt Hanseatic centre with maritime history and easy access to Baltic seaside stretches.

cities.name: Poznań
cities.summary: Poznań is a lively western Polish city of merchant squares, cathedral history and a strong student atmosphere.

cities.name: Zakopane
cities.summary: Zakopane is Poland's mountain capital, good for wooden-villa charm, cable cars and Tatra hiking or winter sports.

cities.name: Katowice
cities.summary: Katowice surprises with strong contemporary culture, Silesian industrial heritage and a compact, improving centre.

cities.name: Toruń
cities.summary: Toruń offers a richly preserved Gothic old town, Copernicus heritage and famous gingerbread in a compact riverside setting.

cities.name: Lublin
cities.summary: Lublin has one of Poland's most atmospheric eastern old towns, plus important multicultural and wartime history.
